history.reason: Two recent verified OzBargain threads (Apr and Nov 2026) ask exactly this, and the replies converge on a rule (grinder first, dual boiler only for heavy milk use). It is a machine-level decision for a different reader than the grinder guide. The writer should link to the grinder guide rather than repeat it.

The decision can be answered from supported claims. Manufacturer pages and booklets show four things. The Express uses a single thermocoil that has to heat for steam and purge afterwards. The Pro uses a ThermoJet that heats in 3 seconds. The Dual Boiler brews and steams at the same time and has no grinder, so leaving the Express means buying a grinder as well. The Oracle Jet automates grind, dose, tamp and milk on a ThermoJet, not a boiler, while the Oracle Dual Boiler adds dual boilers. The grinder-first path rests on Breville's own fast-shot troubleshooting and the earlier grinder research. Owner threads support the rule that a dual boiler is mainly for milk-drink volume and that the grinder should come first. No measured steaming times exist, so the post has to frame steaming waits as a symptom the owner recognises, not a number.
